claim: After v3, the retired list is GC-private: writers make condemned decisions through per-hash `.meta` point reads and do not read `RetiredSet`.
Before the retired-in-snapshot change, each GC folding round performs one GET of the prior retired artifact and one PUT of the next retired artifact per GC shard.

The retired-in-snapshot design removes the `RetiredSet` object, `CART` magic, `Layout::retiredKey`, and `GcState::retired_refs`, and changes settlement from a three-cursor merge to a two-cursor merge.

Retired-in-snapshot preserves settlement semantics including condemn, carry, round-paced graduation, `delete_pending`, redelete, clamp suppression, the pre-CAS single delete site, resurrect-supersede, `.meta` writes, B170 events, and GC-log counters.
Retired-in-snapshot does not change round pacing or the one-round graduation gap, because that gap is the racing-writer edge-surfacing window under EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE.

A `kCondemned` run row has type byte `0x02`, uses the sentinel key `(blob_hash, source_id = 0)`, and encodes flags with bit 0 for `delete_pending`, `token_type`, `condemn_round`, `size`, `token_len`, and token bytes.

`kCondemned` persists the full token type: `ETag = 1`, `Generation = 2`, and `Emulated = 3`; decoding fails with `CORRUPTED_DATA` for an unknown `token_type` or a payload length inconsistent with `token_len`.
A condemned row subsumes the zero marker, while a plain `kZeroMarker` is emitted only when the object is absent at condemnation and remains transient for the generation.
The sentinel key with `source_id = 0` sorts before all real edges of the same blob, allowing the merge cursor to settle condemned state at blob close-out.
A carried `kCondemned` row is settlement-only and must not set the merge touch bit; only real edges or deltas touching a blob may trigger a zero marker or a resurrect-supersede `peek_head` probe.
`source_id = 0` is reserved for sentinel rows: `sourceEdgeId` must throw `LOGICAL_ERROR` on a zero result and delta producers must reject `source_id == 0`.
Source-edge run headers use `key_schema = 1` for `RunKind::SourceEdge`, and every consumer must validate `kind == SourceEdge`, `key_schema == 1`, and row payload lengths through a typed open path.

The typed source-edge run opener rejects an active edge with `source_id = 0`, a zero marker or condemned row with a nonzero source id, unknown row types, and more than one sentinel row per blob with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
`CasFoldSeal` contains a per-GC-shard `condemned_summary` with `condemned_total`, `pending_total`, and `oldest_nonpending_condemn_round`, where `UINT64_MAX` means no nonpending condemned row.
Each shard's `CondemnedSummary` is derived solely from that shard's written run bytes, making the summary a deterministic function of the sealed artifact.
New seals have a total `condemned_summary` map over `gc_shards`; pure ref-carry shards copy the parent summary entry verbatim, and a missing entry is an integrity signal rather than zero.
`graduationDue` is computed from seal summaries as `pending_total > 0 || oldest_nonpending_condemn_round < current_round` and requires zero retired-list I/O.
For `snap_generation > 0`, a missing or undecodable adopted seal, or a seal without `condemned_summary`, makes `graduationDue` return true so the forced fold surfaces the integrity loss.
A shard may be pure-ref-carried only when it has no deltas and `condemned_total == 0`.
`GcState::retired_refs` is removed and its protobuf field number is reserved; `GcState` retains round, fence, shard, snapshot, manifest-sweep, and lease fields without retired-object references.

The two-cursor merge settles a pending row by exact-token redelete at d = 0, spares any row at d > 0, graduates a nonpending row when `condemn_round < current_round`, and otherwise carries it unchanged.

Fresh zero transitions mint a `kCondemned` row from the `head_blob` observation; an absent object produces only a plain `kZeroMarker`, and clamp suppression carries pending rows unchanged while keeping floor-passed rows condemned-only.

`RetiredMergeResult` remains the interface for `graduated`, `spared`, `redelete`, and `replaced` outcomes, which continue to drive outcome logs, `.meta` transitions, B170 events, and `entries_condemned`, `entries_graduated`, and `entries_redeleted` counters.
Destructive redelete actions may execute only for `delete_pending` rows read from the prior durably adopted run; a fresh `head_blob` observation is write-only until durable adoption.

Run and seal adoption continue to use `putDeterministicArtifact`: `putIfAbsent` collisions must be byte-equal or fail with `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and `gc/state` adopts the generation and attempt through the seal.
Artifact keys are pinned to `attempt = lease.seq`, and renew or steal paths bump `lease.seq` every round, so a same-key collision can only be a byte-identical resend within the same attempt.
A divergent artifact under an attempt-pinned key is rejected as `CORRUPTED_DATA`; the round aborts and the next round refolds under a fresh attempt instead of adopting stale edge bytes.

The retired-in-snapshot design explicitly scopes its no-divergence guarantee per attempt: pre-CAS `.meta` and event effects from a deposed leader may remain after an unadopted attempt, as in the prior implementation.
A crash between run PUT and seal or state CAS leaves orphan attempt-scoped artifacts that retention prunes through `snap_pruned_through` under B174.

`previewDeletes` emits every carried `kCondemned` row using its stored token, token type, condemn round, and pending flag, classifying it as `delete_pending` or awaiting graduation without a HEAD probe.
Rebuild must list physical blobs and mint orphan `kCondemned` rows before flushing per-shard runs, because in-run condemned state cannot be added after the run is flushed.
The retired-in-snapshot design keeps B170 events, GC-log counters, `.meta` writes, and the `system.content_addressed_garbage_collection_log` schema unchanged.
A deposed leader can leave a durable stray-Clean meta over a still-`delete_pending` blob when `clearSparedMeta` completes before the leader loses the `gc/state` CAS.
Stray-Clean meta lets a writer reuse the condemned exact token, allowing a later pending `deleteExact` to delete the live reuse and violate `INV_NO_LOSS`.
Moving `clearSparedMeta` after the winning `gc/state` CAS is insufficient because an older leader can execute a stale pre-CAS `deleteExact` after a newer leader adopts a spare and clears the meta.
GC freshness metadata is add-only: GC may publish `Condemned` and remove metadata after confirmed deletion, but GC must never transition `Condemned` to `Clean` on a spare.

Only a writer that has displaced the body with a fresh incarnation token may publish `Clean`, through `uploadFromSource` with `writeResurrectMetaClean` or tokenless committed-source `copyForwardFromCondemned`.
Once a hash is `Condemned`, observing `Clean` means either the condemned body is absent or a writer has already changed its incarnation token.
A spared hash may remain `Condemned` indefinitely; normal reads do not consult the marker, and the next `putBlob` must materialize or copy-forward a fresh incarnation before publishing `Clean`.
The add-only freshness-meta fix removes one spare-side meta GET and CAS per spared entry and adds no per-delete I/O.

The deposed-leader stray-Clean defect was fixed by removing the spare-side clear; the recorded code gate passed the full `Cas*` battery at 542/542 and the TLA gate reported an honest green model with `post_adoption_clear` red.
A CAS pool may contain blobs under several hash algorithms without migration or rehashing; old blobs retain their original algorithm and new writes use the configured algorithm.

The immutable blob identity in a mixed-algorithm pool is the pair `BlobRef{algo, digest}`; a bare digest is not a blob identity and equal digest values under different algorithms name different objects.
`BlobRef` may be constructed only when the algorithm and digest are born together at the write mint or read together by a durable-form parser; all other code copies an existing `BlobRef`.
A blob's `(algo, digest)` identity is immutable from upload through exact-token deletion, so changing the configured write algorithm does not rehash an existing blob.
Mixed manifests store one `BlobRef ref` per `ManifestEntry`; the entry payload is `placement u8, algo u8, digest <lenFor(algo)> raw BE bytes, blob_size u64, inline_len u32, inline`.
The per-manifest `blob_hash_len` header is removed in mixed-algorithm pools, and an unknown entry algorithm fails decoding with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
A new algorithm is admitted only with explicit `<blob_hash_allow_new>1</blob_hash_allow_new>` opt-in; reopening with an unadmitted algorithm and no flag fails with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`.
`PoolMeta.algos_used` is a canonically sorted, append-only set of every algorithm ever admitted to the pool; once an algorithm is admitted, subsequent opens with it need no flag.
The write algorithm is node-local `PoolConfig`/`Store` state and is not persisted as a single pool-wide value, because live nodes may intentionally write with different already-admitted algorithms.

Before writing any blob, manifest, or ref naming an algorithm, a node must durably CAS-union that algorithm into `algos_used`; the union loop rereads after conflicts and recomputes from the fresh value.

A validator with a stale local `algos_used` cache refreshes `_pool_meta` on every miss for a known algorithm and accepts only if the authoritative set contains it; an unknown-to-the-build algorithm remains `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`.
Settlement uses source-edge key schema 3 with key bytes `algo(u8) ++ digest[blobHashLenFor(algo)] ++ source_id(16 BE)`, producing 33-byte keys for 16-byte algorithms and 49-byte keys for SHA-256.
Settlement is not partitioned by algorithm: mixed rows remain in the same `gc_shards` runs, and schemas 1 and 2 plus digest-only settlement helpers are deleted without compatibility shims.
Schema-3 settlement keys are ordered as `(algo, digest, source_id)` because the algorithm byte precedes variable-width digest bytes; the zero-source sentinel sorts first within each blob group.

`SourceEdgeKeyCodec` derives digest length from the algorithm byte, rejects unknown algorithms with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, and rejects a known algorithm with the wrong total key length using `CORRUPTED_DATA`.

Settlement has no algorithm loop: rows are self-describing, `blobShard` uses the first eight digest bytes in big-endian order modulo `gc_shards`, and the algorithm is ignored only inside the shard calculation.
The fold seal remains total over `gc_shards` and gains no algorithm dimension or algorithm-driven partition iteration.
Condemn-sweep and fsck derive algorithm and digest width from the `blobs/<algo>/...` path segment; a segment not in `algos_used` is skipped by sweep and reported as `unaccounted` by fsck.
Deduplication is keyed by `BlobRef` and therefore works only within one algorithm subset; equal content written under different algorithms naturally has different keys and does not cross-deduplicate.
Blob identities in inspect output and event logs render as `algo:hex`, such as `sha256:ab...`, rather than bare hexadecimal.
Mixed-algorithm pools do not rehash existing blobs, perform cross-algorithm deduplication, support per-table or per-insert algorithm selection, or remove algorithms from `algos_used`.

A pre-existing `RunFileReader::seek` bug can skip an exact full key duplicated across a block boundary because it selects the last block with `min_key <= target`; the independent fix is to select the first block with `max_key >= target`.
The selectable blob hash defaults to `cityHash128` v1.0.2 and adds `xxh3-128` and `sha256`; the algorithm is encoded in blob paths and the feature is pre-release with no data migration.
The disk setting `blob_hash` accepts `cityhash128`, `xxh3-128`, or `sha256`; unknown values fail with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`, and Phase 1 rejects `sha256` with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` until Phase 2.
Blob keys use `blobs/<algo>/<2-char-shard>/<hex digest>`, with `<algo>` equal to `ch128`, `xxh3`, or `sha256`; the `.meta` key is the blob key plus `.meta` and staging keys are unchanged.
The `hash_algo` envelope field records the blob's `BlobHashAlgo`; it is a defensive consistency check, while `PoolMeta` and the path segment are authoritative.
`HashingWriteBuffer` checksums for run files and manifests remain `cityHash128`; only the blob content address is selectable.
With no `blob_hash` setting or with `cityhash128`, blob hash values and keys remain byte-for-byte identical to the existing cityHash128 convention.
The recommended default layout includes the `ch128` path segment rather than retaining the legacy no-segment cityHash128 layout, because CA has no persisted-data compatibility requirement.
The Phase 2 digest representation is `BlobDigest` with `std::array<uint8_t,32>` bytes, big-endian ordering, and zero-filled tail bytes beyond the pool's meaningful digest length.
Only the content digest widens for SHA-256; `payload_digest`, `RunRef.checksum`, `sourceEdgeId`, lease owners, heartbeat owners, and `manifestCleanupShard` remain `UInt128` internal identifiers.
`blobShard` for variable-length digests is the big-endian uint64 represented by the first eight digest bytes modulo `gc_shards`, preserving routing for existing 128-bit digests.

Before the variable-length digest port, `CasGc.cpp` condemn-sweep and several `CasFsck.cpp` listing sites used `hexToU128` inside `catch(...) { continue; }`, silently classifying every SHA-256 blob as foreign and causing a permanent leak or false-clean fsck result.
A table's durable ref state is `latest table snapshot + table transaction logs after that snapshot`; snapshots are complete table states and each log object is one atomic writer transaction.

For a table snapshot `S_X`, recovery computes `TableState = Replay(S_X.state, tail(X))`, where `tail(X)` contains every valid log transaction with identifier greater than `X`; without a snapshot, recovery starts from the empty state and `namespace_birth`.
The writer owns table semantics and snapshots, while GC owns ref-log folding and physical cleanup; ordinary writer mutations do not read `gc/state` or wait for a GC round.
GC stores one `last_folded_ref_id` cursor per table and manifest-edge deltas, not complete table state or owners; the cursor map is O(number of tables), not O(number of refs).

Snapshot coverage and GC fold coverage are independent: snapshot `X` lets a writer omit logs through `X`, while the folded cursor proves that those logs no longer need to be read for edge discovery; both are required before log deletion.

`RefTxnId` is `{ writer_epoch: UInt64, ref_sequence: UInt64 }`; both fields are nonzero, writer epochs strictly increase on successful mounts, and `ref_sequence` is strictly increasing within a mounted writer epoch.
The canonical `RefTxnId` rendering is two lower-case fixed-width 16-digit hexadecimal numbers separated by `-`, such as `0000000000000007-000000000000008e`; noncanonical forms are rejected.
A snapshot reuses the `RefTxnId` of its last included log, producing one shared ordered timeline where `log X == snapshot X` and later logs have greater identifiers.
`RefTxnId` is distinct from `build_sequence` and `build_id`; a build may create multiple ref transactions and transactions may contain operations from multiple builds.
Manifest paths use `cas/manifests/<namespace>/<writer-epoch>-<build-sequence>/<ordinal>.proto`, and every manifest, ref-log, inspection, and repair path uses shared canonical parsing and rendering.
Ref objects are laid out under `cas/refs/<namespace>/` as `_cleanup/<remove-txn-id>`, `_log/<txn-id>`, and `_snap/<snapshot-id>.proto`; `_log` sorts before `_snap`.
Snapshot and log bodies are deterministic and repeat key-derived identity fields; a snapshot is never renamed or copied when created, and logs remain under their original keys.
The `_cleanup/<remove-txn-id>` object is a zero-byte completion marker published with `putIfAbsent` after the exact namespace cleanup reaches `Completed`; Phase 1 never deletes markers.
A `Removed` snapshot contains no committed refs or precommits, and a later `namespace_birth` with a greater `RefTxnId` recreates the namespace on the same timeline.
Snapshot rows are sorted by canonical bytewise `ref_name`, then by `ManifestRef`; duplicate rows, noncanonical names, invalid identifiers, and unsorted fields are rejected.

State-growing operations are admitted only if both the encoded snapshot and encoded namespace-removal transaction remain below their respective hard budgets; an oversized operation fails closed before object creation.

Phase 1 uses exactly one body-only log encoding at `_log/<txn-id>`; ref names are not encoded in object keys and invalid relative paths, including empty, `.`, `..`, repeated separators, NUL bytes, and noncanonical escaping, are rejected.
Namespace recreation after `remove_namespace` requires the `_cleanup/<remove-txn-id>` marker for the exact removal transaction; an empty physical prefix is not sufficient.
Promotion removes an exact precommit and creates the committed binding to the same manifest in one transaction, installing the complete initial mutable payload without an ownerless interval.

Replacing an existing committed ref requires an explicit `owner_transition` removal before promotion; silent displacement is forbidden because GC derives edges from explicit operations rather than state diffs.
`remove_namespace` is the final operation in its transaction, follows exact owner transitions for every committed ref and precommit, requires empty owner sets, and records its own `remove_txn_id`.

The namespace-removal transaction emits no additional manifest-edge delta because its preceding exact owner transitions already emit all edge removals; its final operation creates the GC namespace-cleanup request.

Writer startup recovery performs one namespace `LIST`, selects the greatest valid snapshot, GETs it, GETs and replays later logs in `RefTxnId` order, then caches the complete state before enabling mutations.

If a selected snapshot or tail body disappears between recovery `LIST` and `GET`, the writer restarts with a fresh `LIST`; absence is not corruption and recovery never falls back to an older plausible snapshot.
At most one ref-log PUT per table may have an unresolved result; a later same-table PUT cannot start until the earlier result is resolved.

An uncertain ref-log create is never treated as failed when an exact-key GET finds absence; the append lane remains wedged until identical bytes are observed, a whitelisted definite rejection is proven, or the writer unmounts.
A `PreconditionFailed` ref-log create always resolves through exact-key observation: identical bytes mean success of the earlier attempt, while different bytes are corruption.
A predecessor PUT that completes after successor recovery can create a late older-epoch log invisible to the successor and later snapshots; a missed `+1` edge is a data-loss class, not merely a leak.
`snapshot_min_log_age_ms` delays snapshot coverage of young logs to reduce the late-predecessor completion window, but it is a wall-clock risk reduction and not a correctness proof.
Warm table mutations perform no ref `LIST`, snapshot GET, `gc/state` read, HEAD, or compare-and-swap; they append one deterministic log object and update cached state.
Failed precommit cleanup is persisted by the writer before build retirement; GC does not detect or remove dead precommits by itself.
Live snapshots are published only by the writer from its complete cached state; GC never reconstructs table state and may publish only the constant-size `Removed` snapshot for a removed namespace.
A writer publishes a snapshot when log count or log bytes exceed thresholds, or after mount recovery exceeds a threshold; publication is off the mutation hot path and never blocks appends.
The snapshot published by the writer is an integrity oracle: fsck can replay the snapshot and tail and compare the deterministic bytes, with divergence treated as corruption.
GC performs one paginated global `LIST cas/refs/` per round for ref intake, snapshot observation, and cleanup planning; it does not perform per-table LISTs or snapshot HEADs.
GC resumes pagination exactly after the last key returned by the previous page; opaque continuation tokens are usable only when the backend documents equivalent positioning semantics.
A ref fold aborts without partial delta or destructive authorization when a key, transaction body, operation, or input-visibility condition is malformed or ambiguous.

Owner transitions emit direct manifest-edge events: owner addition is `+1`, removal is `-1`, same-manifest promotion is neutral, replacement emits old `-1` and new `+1`, and mutable-payload updates emit no edge.
Ref intake never directly deletes blobs or manifests; it only feeds appeared and disappeared edges to the existing multi-round GC settlement and delayed-delete protocol.
A ref log is eligible for deletion only when the durable per-table fold cursor covers it, a snapshot observed by the same scan covers it, and any namespace-removal cleanup work is durable.
Namespace cleanup has durable `Pending` and terminal `Completed` states keyed by `{namespace, remove_txn_id}`; `Completed` is written only after a pass observes no remaining objects to delete.

Namespace cleanup deletes only exact keys captured by its own enumeration and never uses a prefix wildcard; after recreation, exact keys from the removed incarnation cannot name newly created objects.
The writer consumes only the `_cleanup/<remove-txn-id>` marker as the namespace cleanup completion signal; a physically empty prefix is not authoritative.

An orphan-manifest sweep uses the newest snapshot plus every later log, including manifests removed in the tail, and additionally requires the durable `last_folded_ref_id` before deleting a retired manifest.

For one GC round, ref-specific request cost is approximately `LIST_pages(Q) + 0.08 * (K + H)` under the stated S3 Standard request-price ratio, where `K` is new log GETs and `H` is manifest-body cache misses.
GC ref-intake memory is O(one LIST page plus a bounded decoded transaction batch, emitted edge buffer, and retained exact cleanup keys), independent of table size.

If GC loses its cursor state, writer recovery remains valid because snapshots and logs are authoritative; destructive GC stays disabled until an explicit offline rebuild establishes a verified current-owner baseline.
Phase 1 rejects a global ref-sequence watermark because lexical scan order differs from sequence order across tables and a global watermark could mark unseen concurrent appends as folded.
S3-native staging is opt-in per disk and off by default; large blobs stream to `POOL/staging/<mount_id>/<rnd>.tmp`, then promote to the content key by write-once conditional server-side copy.
The default `cas_staging_backend=local` path is byte-for-byte the existing `scratchPath()` path; it performs no capability probe and takes no S3 staging branch.

`cas_staging_backend` accepts `local` or `s3`, and `cas_s3_staging_min_bytes` defaults to approximately 64 MiB; blobs below the threshold remain on the local path and inline blobs at or below `INLINE_CAP` are unaffected.
S3 staging promotion must use `If-None-Match:*` on `CopyObject` and on `CompleteMultipartUpload`; unconditional overwrite is forbidden.
Unconditional staging-to-blob copy is unsafe because the read path does not rehash bodies, so overwriting a live object can expose a torn or short body as valid data.
Racing multipart copies can produce different multipart ETags, leaving the losing writer's recorded token stale and making exact-token deletion unable to reclaim the object.
A dedup shortcut that adopts an existing blob after HEAD without the condemn check can reference a blob pending GC deletion and violate edge-before-observe, causing data loss.
The staging capability probe must perform a conditional copy and demand a real 412 on a second copy; support of conditional `PutObject` alone does not prove conditional-copy support.
Any conditional-copy probe error or non-enforcing result selects local staging and logs that S3 staging is unavailable; it must never silently fall back to unconditional overwrite.

The S3 staging lifecycle is `precommitAdd(edge) → stage → promote(copy)+condemn-check → delete staging → promoteBuild(visible)`; a manifest cannot become visible before the blob exists at its content key.

On a successful conditional copy, the destination ETag from `CopyObject` or `CompleteMultipartUpload` becomes the blob incarnation token; on `PreconditionFailed`, the writer HEADs the destination and executes the existing condemn/resurrect gate.
If the existing destination is condemned, resurrection copies from the writer's staging object and never reads or copies the condemned blob key as the resurrection source.
A staging object is deleted only after promotion and the condemn check complete, because it remains the resurrection source during that gate.
A crash between copy completion and staging deletion may leak a staging object, which is reclaimed by a lease-fenced sweeper scoped to the mount's `staging/<mount_id>/` prefix and by GC age sweeps.
If a mount lease expires, the writer is fenced and a subsequent staging-source 404 must fail closed by aborting the insert rather than committing.
Recovery must not promote a precommit whose staged copy is not verifiably complete; it must re-drive promotion from the surviving staging object or abort recovery of that build.
GC discovers blobs by listing `blobs/`, so it excludes `staging/`; the staging sweeper is the only reclaimer of staging objects and GC must not exact-token-delete them as orphan blobs.
The optional memory fast path is a separable optimization: small S3-mode blobs may be buffered in memory and written with `putIfAbsentStream`, while large blobs use S3 staging and conditional copy.

The Native CAS backend exposes `supportsConditionalCopy()`, `stageStream(staging_key)`, and `promoteStaged(staging_key, blob_key)`; Local and Emulated backends report unsupported and use local staging.
S3-native staging keeps reads content-hash-only: no read or fsck path may gate on an ETag or token, because multipart ETags are not content MD5 values.

The unattended campaign recorded that the S3-staging implementation was opt-in, capability-probed, and validated on RustFS after an end-to-end test caught missing `CABL` envelope bytes that in-memory tests did not expose.

The unattended campaign recorded Phase 2 SHA-256 support as a completed variable-length digest implementation with real-S3 validation of `blobs/sha256/<64hex>`, exact-token reclamation, and `dangling==0`.

The unattended campaign recorded the retired-in-snapshot refactor as soak-validated with `dangling==0` at every phase-3 checkpoint and the add-only deposed-leader fix as TLA-gated with `post_adoption_clear` red.

The add-only TLA model requires both adopting `FoldRound` and deposed `FoldAbort` folds to leave meta unchanged on spare, while only writer fresh-upload or resurrection may change present `Condemned` to `Clean` with a token change.
The add-only safety gate uses split two-leader actions—capture snapshot, execute pre-CAS side effects including `deleteExact`, then attempt adoption—to expose stale-redelete races.

The old `gc_clear_on_spare` behavior and the post-adoption clear modeled by `post_adoption_clear` must remain red in the TLA gate; the latter is specifically unsafe because adoption does not fence pre-CAS side effects.

The two-leader regression must verify that after a spare the marker remains `Condemned`, a writer resurrects to a fresh token `t2`, and stale `deleteExact(t1)` returns `TokenMismatch` or `Replaced` without removing the live body.
Removing the spare-side `scheduleMetaJob(... clearSparedMeta ...)` call requires no meta format change, no new I/O, and no delete-path change; `writeCondemnedMeta` and `deleteConfirmedMeta` remain.

The mixed-algorithm implementation deletes `kSourceEdgeKeySchema128`, `kSourceEdgeKeySchemaSha256`, `sourceEdgeDigestLen`, and `sourceEdgeKeySchemaFor`; there is one self-describing schema-3 settlement key codec.

The mixed-algorithm implementation retypes `BlobDelta`, `BlobCandidate`, `RetiredEntry`, `OutcomeEntry`, `.meta` APIs, dedup-cache keys, and pending dependencies to `BlobRef` rather than retaining digest-only identity overloads.

The Phase 2 SHA-256 implementation must port the `CasGc.cpp` condemn sweep and `CasFsck.cpp` listing sites in the same change that widens the digest; otherwise the pool silently leaks every SHA-256 blob.
The Phase 2 digest codec must reject wrong-width hex or byte input with `BAD_ARGUMENTS` and assert that tail bytes beyond a 16-byte pool digest are zero.

The S3 staging plan requires `ConditionalCopyResult{created, dest_etag}` and makes unsupported conditional copy throw or select local staging rather than provide a non-enforcing default implementation.
For S3 staging, `publishStaging` must run the same `putBlob` condemn/resurrect gate as local staging; the only changed upload primitive is conditional server-side copy from the staging object.
The staging sweeper exposes `sweepOwnMountOnStart()` and `ageSweep(now, ttl)`, both lease-fenced so an in-flight staging object younger than TTL is not deleted.
